mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises by > 0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A pronounced deceleration in real GDP growth (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters, accompanied by a decline in housing starts (HOUST), indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > 1.5% q/q for two consecutive quarters AND HOUST falls > 10% q/q
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 and HOUST meet the specified declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over three consecutive months, without a corresponding decline in unemployment, signals supply-side disruptions that raise input costs and depress earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 2% for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE does not rise > 0.2% in the same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when INDPRO declines > 2% for three months without a rise in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals an emergency easing response to a financial shock, which boosts liquidity and risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops > 0.75% in one month to below 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS drops > 0.75% in one month to below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal income (implied from PAYEMS growth) and a surge in retail sales (implied from RSAFS growth) over two months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both rise > 1% m/m for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both PAYEMS and RSAFS rise > 1% m/m for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months, with stable wage growth (implied by labor market tightness), signals a tight labor market that increases wage inflation and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit margins erode.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE remains below 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) over two months, without a corresponding spike in unemployment, signals a supply-side recovery that boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both rise > 1% m/m for two consecutive months AND UNRATE does not rise > 0.2% in the same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when INDPRO and HOUST both rise > 1% m/m for two months without a rise in UNRATE.
